transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I keep blowing up at people over nothing. I’m snapping on operations calls, and even at my family, and… that’s just not how I usually handle things. It’s gotten bad enough that I figured I needed to talk to someone.
Have you always had a tendency to snap at people or is this a relatively new behavior for you?

No, this is new for me. I mean, I’ve gotten irritated like anyone, but I don’t usually blow up at people. Lately I’m snapping on operations calls and even at my family over small stuff, and that’s just not how I’ve ever handled things.
How long have you been experiencing these episodes of snapping at people?
About three weeks now. It started after the valve failure and the injury at the facility, and it’s been happening since then.
Do you feel irritable or on edge even when you're not snapping at people?

Yeah. Even when I’m not actually yelling or snapping, I feel kind of wound up. Like I’m already irritated and it doesn’t take much to set me off. Then on calls or at home, something small happens and I blow up over it.
Have you been feeling sad or depressed most of the time since you started snapping at people?
I don’t know if I’d call it depressed most of the time. I’ve been upset and worn down, yeah, but I haven’t really thought of it as feeling sad all day. The irritability is what I notice more.
Have you been feeling anxious a lot since these episodes of snapping at people started?

Yeah, I have. It’s like I’m on alert all the time. If I hear a forklift beep, or a compressor kick on, even the smoke alarm chirping at home, my whole body tightens up. I start looking around for exits or thinking about what could go wrong next.
Have you been avoiding certain places or situations since the valve failure and injury at the facility?
I’m not sure. I mean, I don’t think I’ve been making a list of places to avoid or anything. I just… I haven’t really paid attention to it that way.
Have you been having any memories or images of the valve failure and injury at the facility that feel really vivid or disturbing to you?

Yes. It happens out of nowhere. I can be sitting at the kitchen table or trying to get through emails at home, and suddenly I’m seeing that flash from the valve again, and the smoke in the aisle. It feels really vivid, like it pushes everything else out of my head for a bit.
Are there any places or situations that you've been avoiding since the incident at the facility?
I’m honestly not sure. I haven’t really thought of it as avoiding places. I guess I just go where I have to go and try not to think about it too much.
Have you found yourself deliberately staying away from anything that reminds you of the valve failure and injury at the facility?
I don’t know that I’m deliberately staying away from anything. I mean, I might be without realizing it, but I haven’t noticed myself making a point to avoid reminders.
Have you been going out of your way to avoid things that remind you of the incident at the facility?
I don’t think so. I mean, I’m not going out of my way on purpose, at least not that I’ve noticed. I just try to get through the day and not dwell on it.
Do you find yourself avoiding talking or thinking about the valve failure and injury at the facility?

I’m not really sure. I don’t sit down and decide, “I’m not going to talk about it,” but I guess I don’t bring it up much. If it comes up, I try to answer and move on. Thinking about it… I don’t know, I just try not to stay on it too long.
Do you have trouble falling or staying asleep since the incident at the facility?

Yes. Most nights I just lie there, and it’s like I can still hear that alarm in my head. When I finally fall asleep, I wake up sweating from dreams about the smoke and people yelling. By morning it feels like I barely slept at all.
Has your irritability or these episodes of snapping at people caused any problems for you at work or in your relationships with family or friends?

Yes. I haven’t been cleared to go back to the plant, and even from home I’m not doing well. I miss things on calls, lose my patience, and people can tell. I’ve upset a few folks, and honestly I’m worried I’m turning into a liability instead of the manager they need.
Do you find yourself avoiding people, places, or activities that remind you of the valve failure and injury at the facility?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really been going many places anyway, so I don’t know if I’m avoiding them on purpose. I guess I haven’t noticed a clear pattern with people or activities.
Do you find yourself avoiding people, places, or activities that remind you of the valve failure and injury at the facility?

Like I said, I’m not really sure. I haven’t been out much, so it’s hard to tell if I’m actually avoiding certain places or people, or if I’m just staying home. Nothing really specific stands out to me.
Are there specific people, places, or things that you're making an effort to avoid because they remind you of the incident at the facility?

I don’t know that I can point to anything specific. I mean, I haven’t really been putting myself around much, so maybe I am avoiding things without thinking about it, but I haven’t noticed a certain person or place that I’m deliberately staying away from.
Are you making an effort to avoid thoughts or memories of the valve failure and injury at the facility?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I don’t sit there trying to think about it, but I don’t know if I’m actively pushing it away either. I haven’t noticed myself making a real effort one way or the other.
